questions.explain: Frequencies below 20 Hz are infrasound; above 20 kHz, ultrasound.

questions.prompt: A submarine’s SONAR detects an echo from another vessel 2 s after sending a pulse. How far away is it? (v = 1500 m/s)

questions.explain: Below 20 Hz: infrasound. 20 Hz – 20 kHz: audible. Above 20 kHz: ultrasound.

questions.prompt: Explain how a ship uses SONAR to find the depth of the sea, including the calculation.
questions.modelAnswer: A transmitter on the ship sends a short pulse of ultrasound down into the water. It reflects off the sea bed and the echo is picked up by a detector on the ship, which measures the time t between sending and receiving. The pulse travels down and back, so depth = speed of sound in water × t ÷ 2. For example, with v = 1500 m/s and t = 2 s, the depth is 1500 m.
rubric: Ultrasound pulse sent down and reflected from the sea bed
Depth = v × t ÷ 2 (halved for the return trip)
